reason: E2 confirms that Laves phase fraction decreases with increasing SPS temperature (21.5 vol.% at 1300°C vs. 11.5 vol.% at 1400°C) and mentions coarsening of oxides at higher temperature, but does not explicitly state grain size refinement of the BCC matrix. E1 states that fine-grained Laves phases protect against wear and that increasing SPS temperature coarsens Laves phases, increasing wear, but does not address corrosion resistance or the specific quantitative predictions. The corrosion premise and the exact 40%/30% improvements are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Lower SPS temperature (1300°C) yields a fine-grained BCC matrix with a higher fraction of finely dispersed Laves phases.
Higher SPS temperature (1400°C) yields a coarser microstructure with a lower fraction of Laves phases.
Fine-grained BCC matrix with finely dispersed Laves phases provides higher hardness and wear resistance.
Fine-grained BCC matrix with finely dispersed Laves phases provides better corrosion resistance (passive film integrity).
The microstructural differences will result in ~40% lower wear and ~30% lower corrosion for the 1300°C sample.
